name: pyyaml

ground_truth.breaks: TypeError: load() missing 1 required positional argument: 'Loader'
ground_truth.source: PyYAML 6.0 changelog: Loader is a required argument of load/load_all (deprecated with YAMLLoadWarning since 5.1)
ground_truth.note: The right Loader is a judgment call (safe_load vs FullLoader); the app only needs plain data so the manual migration picks safe_load. Control: yaml.load(s, Loader=yaml.FullLoader) at load_trusted and yaml.load(s, Loader=FastSafeLoader) at load_fast are unchanged and must NOT be flagged.

verified.old: 5.4.1 (py3.11): works with the FullLoader-like default, emits YAMLLoadWarning ('calling yaml.load() without Loader=... is deprecated, as the default Loader is unsafe')
verified.new: 6.0.2 (py3.12): TypeError: load() missing 1 required positional argument: 'Loader'

ground_truth.breaks: TypeError: load_all() missing 1 required positional argument: 'Loader'

verified.new: 6.0.2: TypeError as above; yaml.safe_load_all returns the same documents

ground_truth.breaks: AttributeError: module 'yaml' has no attribute 'YAMLLoadWarning' (when load_settings_quiet runs)
ground_truth.source: PyYAML 6.0 (the warning class went away together with the no-Loader fallback)

verified.old: 5.4.1: yaml.YAMLLoadWarning exists (a RuntimeWarning subclass); filtering it silences the load warning

ground_truth.breaks: TypeError caught by the app's own try/except, so load_override() silently returns None instead of the parsed mapping; the app test only checks that the call does not crash

notes: YAMLLoadWarning is raised by yaml/__init__.py::load_warning via Python-level warnings.warn (verified in the 5.4.1 source), so S2 does NOT bite here. libyaml/CLoader is involved only as a behaviour difference, not a warning: PyYAML 5.4.1 has no py3.11 wheel, so the old env is built from sdist and, without libyaml headers on the host, has no CSafeLoader (`yaml.__with_libyaml__` False), while 6.0.2's wheel bundles libyaml (True). app/settings.py's `try: from yaml import CSafeLoader ... except ImportError: SafeLoader` therefore picks SafeLoader on old and CSafeLoader on new; every test input loads to identical data, but the value of FastSafeLoader.__name__ differs. No warning of any kind comes from C in either env. ENV BUILD NOTE: `uv pip install PyYAML==5.4.1` on py3.11 fails to build with the default isolated build (Cython 3: AttributeError: 'build_ext' object has no attribute 'cython_sources'); it installs with a build constraint, `UV_BUILD_CONSTRAINT=<file containing 'Cython<3'>`. Not reproduced / dropped (verified identical on 5.4.1 and 6.0.2 across ~150 dump/load probes): yaml.dump default sort order, default_flow_style (changed in 5.1, both sides are already after that), sort_keys, indent/width/allow_unicode/canonical, safe_dump of tuples/sets/objects, FullLoader python/* tags, implicit resolvers (octal 010 -> 8 in both). The ONLY 5.4 -> 6.0 differences found are the Loader requirement and the removal of YAMLLoadWarning. Controls that must stay clean: load_trusted (Loader=yaml.FullLoader), load_fast, dump_settings(default_flow_style=False), dump_ordered(sort_keys=False), dump_safe. The change scenario adds a yaml.load(raw) with no Loader inside try/except TypeError; the manual migration edits are phrased so they do not touch it, so after migration it behaves differently (dict -> None) while its test stays green. Identical-behaviour check: original on 5.4.1 and migrated app (safe_load / safe_load_all) on 6.0.2 print the same repr for all loaders and dumpers, except FastSafeLoader name.
